overview: Chagas disease is caused by the infection of a protozoan parasite (Trypanosoma cruzi) and is a complex health problem typical of neglected tropical diseases and socially- and environmentally-determined diseases. Approximately 8 million people worldwide are estimated to be infected with T. cruzi, leading to more than 10,000 deaths every year. Chagas disease is curable if antiparasitic treatment is done early, in the acute phase.
symptoms: purplish swelling of the lids of one eye (Romaña’s sign)
transmission: contact with faeces/urine of infected triatomine bugs
consumption of food or beverages contaminated with T. cruzi
through blood or blood product transfusion
prevention: blood screening prior to transfusion and transplantation
earliest possible diagnosis and comprehensive follow-up and health care
risk_factors: living in endemic areas of 21 continental Latin American countries
key_facts: 8 million people worldwide are estimated to be infected with T. cruzi
100 million people are considered at risk of infection
10,000 new cases of congenital transmission annually
